F2-L05.intro: Make the pair match: masculine and feminine people (طَالِبٌ / طَالِبَةٌ) and adjectives that follow and agree (طَالِبَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ). Describe people and things — and spot the mistake when they don’t match.

tasks.task: Say he is a new student.
Say she is a new student — make both words feminine.
Describe the teacher with one adjective.
ASK if the female teacher is kind too (your friend then answers).
tasks.en: And is the (female) teacher kind too?

tasks.task: Answer the unexpected: describe your brother with two adjectives.
tasks.en: My brother is tall and clever.

roleplays.setting: Showing a family photo to your pen-pal
roleplays.title: My family photo

tasks.task: Say who he is and describe him.
tasks.en: This is my father; he is tall and kind.

tasks.task: Say who she is and describe her (feminine).
tasks.en: This is my mother; she is kind and clever.

tasks.task: Say who the little girl is and describe her.
tasks.model: هٰذِهِ أُخْتِي، هِيَ صَغِيرَةٌ وَسَعِيدَةٌ جِدًّا.
tasks.en: This is my sister; she is little and very happy.

tasks.examiner: … هٰذَا بَيْتُ جَدِّي، وَهُوَ بَيْتٌ قَدِيمٌ وَجَمِيلٌ.
tasks.task: ASK your pen-pal what the building in their photo is (they then answer).
tasks.en: And what is this in your photo?

tasks.task: Answer the unexpected question with a contrast.
tasks.model: لَا، أُخْتِي قَصِيرَةٌ، وَلٰكِنَّ أَخِي طَوِيلٌ.
tasks.en: No, my sister is short, but my brother is tall.

tasks.task: Describe your female friend with three matching adjectives.
tasks.en: My friend is clever, kind and always happy.

tasks.help: الخَطَأُ أَنَّ … ؛ يَجِبُ أَنْ أَقُولَ … لِأَنَّ …
tasks.model: الخَطَأُ أَنَّ الصِّفَةَ مُذَكَّرَةٌ؛ يَجِبُ أَنْ أَقُولَ «مُعَلِّمَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ»، لِأَنَّ الاِسْمَ مُؤَنَّثٌ.
tasks.en: The mistake is that the adjective is masculine; I must say “muʿallimatun jadīdatun”, because the noun is feminine.

tasks.examiner: صِفْ شَخْصَيْنِ فِي أُسْرَتِكَ: رَجُلًا وَامْرَأَةً.
tasks.task: Describe a man and a woman in your family, both correctly matched.
tasks.model: جَدِّي رَجُلٌ كَبِيرٌ وَلَطِيفٌ، وَجَدَّتِي امْرَأَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ وَجَمِيلَةٌ.
tasks.en: My grandfather is an old, kind man, and my grandmother is an old, beautiful woman.

tasks.examiner: … لَا؛ بَعْضُ الكَلِمَاتِ مُؤَنَّثَةٌ بِدُونِ «ة»، مِثْلَ «أُمٌّ» وَ«بِنْتٌ».
tasks.task: ASK if all feminine words end in ة (the teacher then answers).
tasks.en: Do all feminine words have tā’ marbūṭa?

tasks.task: Answer the unexpected: describe your school (مَدْرَسَةٌ is feminine!).
tasks.model: مَدْرَسَتِي كَبِيرَةٌ وَجَمِيلَةٌ، وَلٰكِنَّهَا قَدِيمَةٌ قَلِيلًا.
tasks.en: My school is big and beautiful, but it is a little old.

conversation.qen: Are you a (male) student or a (female) student?

conversation.en: My teacher is kind and clever. (f.)

conversation.qen: Describe your brother and your sister.
conversation.model: أَخِي طَوِيلٌ وَسَعِيدٌ، وَأُخْتِي قَصِيرَةٌ وَجَمِيلَةٌ.
conversation.en: My brother is tall and happy, and my sister is short and beautiful.

conversation.qen: Describe two things in your bag.
conversation.en: I have a new book and an old ruler.

conversation.qen: What are the plurals of “ṭālib” and “ṭāliba”?
conversation.en: The plural of “ṭālib” is “ṭullāb”, and of “ṭāliba” is “ṭālibāt”.

conversation.qen: Why do we say “bintun ṣaghīratun” and not “bintun ṣaghīrun”?
conversation.model: لِأَنَّ الصِّفَةَ تُطَابِقُ الاِسْمَ؛ «بِنْتٌ» مُؤَنَّثٌ، فَنُضِيفُ «ـةٌ» إِلَى الصِّفَةِ.
conversation.en: Because the adjective matches the noun; “bint” is feminine, so we add -a to the adjective.

conversation.qen: Describe a male and a female friend with three adjectives each.
conversation.starter: صَدِيقِي … … وَ… وَ… ، وَصَدِيقَتِي … …ـةٌ وَ…ـةٌ وَ…ـةٌ
conversation.model: صَدِيقِي عُمَرُ طَوِيلٌ وَذَكِيٌّ وَلَطِيفٌ، وَصَدِيقَتِي سَارَةُ قَصِيرَةٌ وَذَكِيَّةٌ وَسَعِيدَةٌ.
conversation.en: My friend Omar is tall, clever and kind, and my friend Sara is short, clever and happy.

conversation.qen: Name some feminine words without tā’ marbūṭa.
conversation.model: «أُمٌّ» كَلِمَةٌ مُؤَنَّثَةٌ لَيْسَ فِيهَا «ة»، وَكَذٰلِكَ «بِنْتٌ» وَ«أُخْتٌ».
conversation.en: “Umm” is a feminine word without tā’ marbūṭa, and so are “bint” and “ukht”.

conversation.q: كَيْفَ كُنْتَ وَأَنْتَ صَغِيرٌ، وَكَيْفَ أَنْتَ الآنَ؟
conversation.qen: What were you like when you were little, and what are you like now?
conversation.starter: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا كُنْتُ … ، وَالآنَ أَنَا …
conversation.model: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا كُنْتُ قَصِيرًا، وَالآنَ أَنَا طَوِيلٌ وَسَعِيدٌ فِي مَدْرَسَتِي الجَدِيدَةِ.
conversation.en: When I was little I was short, and now I am tall and happy at my new school.
